entry.title: Routing Bug Puts Solana Within 4.5 Points of Losing Finality
entry.summary: A misconfigured BGP route at hosting provider Teraswitch took 28.83% of staked SOL offline on Wednesday morning, leaving Solana just 4.51 percentage points short of the 33.34% threshold at which the chain stops finalizing transactions. Roughly 90 validators were affected, and networking recovered after about 33 minutes. This incident is a severe stress test for Solana's network stability: a single provider misconfiguration nearly halted the entire chain, exposing how concentrated staked SOL is within one autonomous system. It underscores risks for validators, staking protocols, and the broader ecosystem, and could intensify calls for better decentralization and failover practices. The affected autonomous system, AS20326, holds roughly 27% of staked SOL — above the 25% cap in the Solana Foundation's delegation program — and 94% of it went offline at once. Marinade Finance found that 80.2 million SOL across 59 validators recovered after routing reconverged, while Helius was down for the full 33 minutes; the 333 SOL in lost rewards will be covered by validator bonds.

entry.title: Bybit sues North Korea over $1.5B crypto theft
entry.summary: Bybit has filed a lawsuit against North Korea in connection with the $1.5 billion theft of cryptocurrency from the exchange. This legal action escalates the dispute to a formal court case against a state actor. The lawsuit could set a legal precedent for how cryptocurrency exchanges pursue recovery from state-sponsored hackers. It also highlights the growing intersection of national security, international law, and the digital asset industry. The theft occurred on Bybit's platform and is among the largest cryptocurrency heists ever recorded. The specific legal grounds and jurisdiction for the lawsuit have not yet been publicly disclosed.

entry.title: Solana Nears Finality Halt as 28.83% of Staked SOL Goes Delinquent
entry.summary: On August 12, 2026, a routing failure at infrastructure provider Teraswitch caused 28.83% of staked SOL to go delinquent, bringing Solana 86% of the way to the threshold at which block finality halts. Marinade reported that 94% of the 118.89 million SOL on its autonomous system went offline. The event highlights systemic concentration risk in Solana's validator infrastructure, because a single provider's routing problem nearly threatened network-wide finality. It also directly affected Marinade, Solana's largest liquid staking protocol, and could shake confidence in staking reliability across the ecosystem. Teraswitch confirmed the outage was caused by a routing software failure triggered during a routine configuration change, affecting 12 sites. Solana's finality stops only when more than 33.34% of staked SOL is delinquent, and roughly 90 validators were affected, losing staking rewards.

entry.title: Coldcard Hack Spurs $15B Bitcoin Migration to Self-Custody
entry.summary: A Coldcard firmware exploit that began July 30 drained roughly 2,100 BTC (~$130 million), and onchain data shows 233,000 BTC (~$15 billion) moved out of long-term holder wallets in the following days. Casa CEO Nick Neuman attributes part of that migration to Ledger and Trezor users upgrading to multisig self-custody. The incident underscores that hardware wallet vulnerabilities can be contained by distributed self-custody, and may accelerate multisig adoption among long-term Bitcoin holders. It also shows self-custody adapting under stress, reinforcing Bitcoin's resilience as an asset. Checkonchain data shows 233,000 BTC left long-term holder wallets—a 1.38% drop from recent highs—while 22,000 BTC moved to exchanges. Galaxy Research separately counted roughly 1,596 BTC stolen across more than 5,200 addresses in three attack waves, and the firmware bug had reduced key entropy from 128 bits to about 40 bits.

entry.title: Solana Nearly Freezes After Routing Glitch Offlines 29% of Staked SOL
entry.summary: On Wednesday, a routing glitch traced to Teraswitch's Miami data center knocked nearly 29% of Solana's staked tokens offline, according to staking platform Marinade Finance. The outage lasted about 33 minutes and brought the network to within about 20 million tokens of the one-third staked threshold that halts finality. The incident exposes a serious centralization risk in Solana's staking infrastructure: a single network operator, AS2032, controlled more than a quarter of all staked SOL. Had the offline stake exceeded one-third, the entire chain would have frozen for every SOL holder, raising broader questions about Solana's reliability as a leading smart contract platform. Roughly 90 validators were affected and lost about 333 SOL in rewards, a relatively small sum covered by validator bonds. The bad route from Teraswitch spread to European and Asian data centers, cutting off validators in London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Singapore and Tokyo; North America stayed online, and traffic was restored by 4:16 a.m. UTC.

entry.title: Goldman Sachs to Buy Neos for $2.25B, Adding Bitcoin and Ether ETFs
entry.summary: Goldman Sachs announced it will acquire Neos Investments for up to $2.25 billion. The deal gives Goldman access to Neos's Bitcoin High Income ETF, Boosted Bitcoin High Income ETF, and Ethereum High Income ETF. A top-tier global investment bank is making a dedicated acquisition to own cryptocurrency income-generating ETFs, signaling deeper institutional adoption of digital assets. The move could accelerate mainstream distribution of regulated bitcoin and ether products. The acquisition is valued at up to $2.25 billion. Neos's Bitcoin High Income ETF (BTCI) launched on October 16, 2024, the Boosted Bitcoin High Income ETF (XBCI) launched on January 22, 2026, and the Ethereum High Income ETF (NEHI) uses options and investments in spot Ether ETPs to generate monthly income.

entry.title: Goldman Sachs to acquire ETF manager NEOS in $2.25B deal
entry.summary: Goldman Sachs has agreed to acquire ETF manager NEOS Investments for up to $2.25 billion, adding its $30 billion options-based income ETF business, including Bitcoin- and Ether-linked funds, to Goldman Sachs Asset Management. The acquisition is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approval. This acquisition signals continued institutional adoption of crypto-linked investment products through traditional asset managers. It gives Goldman's clients access to Bitcoin and Ether income-generating ETFs, potentially broadening the institutional investor base for digital assets. NEOS manages 19 options-based income ETFs, including the Bitcoin High Income ETF (BTCI), Boosted Bitcoin High Income ETF (XBCI), and Ethereum High Income ETF (NEHI), which use covered call strategies to generate monthly income. Combined with Goldman's separate purchase of Innovator Capital Management, the deal would bring its global ETF platform to about $130 billion in assets.

entry.title: Goldman's $2.25B NEOS Deal Buys Ready-Made Bitcoin Income ETF Business
entry.summary: Goldman Sachs agreed to acquire NEOS Investments for up to $2.25 billion in a cash-and-equity deal expected to close in Q1 2027. The acquisition brings about $30 billion in options-based income ETFs under Goldman Sachs Asset Management, including the roughly $1 billion BTCI Bitcoin covered-call fund. The deal gives Goldman Sachs a ready-made crypto income ETF business, bypassing the slower path of its own April filing for a Bitcoin Premium ETF. It marks a major institutional adoption signal as derivative-income ETFs—roughly $180 billion in assets—become a fast-growing corner of the market with crypto as an increasingly prominent slice. NEOS's flagship product, BTCI, generates monthly income by selling covered calls on Bitcoin exposure, capping upside in exchange for yield; a similar Ethereum product is also included. Goldman's own April filing for a Bitcoin Premium ETF used a comparable options-writing structure, and the NEOS deal absorbs an established manager rather than waiting for a new fund to gain traction.

entry.title: Goldman Sachs to acquire NEOS Investments in $2.25B bitcoin ETF deal
entry.summary: Goldman Sachs has agreed to acquire NEOS Investments, the manager of the $1.1 billion BTCI bitcoin synthetic ETF, in a cash-and-equity deal valuing NEOS at up to $2.25 billion. The transaction is expected to close in early 2027 pending regulatory approval. This acquisition marks a significant institutional adoption signal, as a top-tier bank acquires a bitcoin income ETF issuer for $2.25 billion. It intensifies competition with BlackRock in the fast-growing derivative income ETF market and underscores bitcoin's growing acceptance within traditional finance. BTCI does not directly hold bitcoin; it uses a covered-call strategy on bitcoin ETPs to generate a yield of about 27%, but has fallen roughly 43% over the past year and charges a 0.99% expense ratio. The deal gives Goldman a $30 billion options-based ETF platform across 19 funds, lifting its total ETF assets above $130 billion.

entry.title: Ravencoin Crashes 20% as Critical Exploit Threatens Multi-Day Rollback
entry.summary: A critical consensus vulnerability was demonstrated and exploited on the Ravencoin network, allowing invalid blocks to be accepted starting at block height 4,487,776 on August 7, 2026. Mining pools controlling a majority of hash power are mining a chain that excludes the exploited branch, which could trigger a deep reorganization of roughly three days, and RVN has crashed 20%. This incident breaks the assumption of transaction finality on a proof-of-work blockchain, putting deposits, withdrawals, and payments made since Friday at risk of reversal. It directly affects Ravencoin holders, exchanges, and users, and raises broader questions about the security implications of hash rate concentration. The first known invalid block appeared at height 4,487,776 on 2026-08-07 15:44:01 UTC, with block 4,487,775 proposed as the last valid block. 2Miners and RavenMiner, which control a majority of network hash rate, declined the developer's request to mine a more recent recovery point, and exchanges Upbit and Bitvavo have already suspended RVN deposits and withdrawals.

entry.title: Anthropic, Riot strike $9B AI compute deal for Texas power
entry.summary: Riot Platforms announced a 20-year agreement to supply 191 megawatts of capacity from its Rockdale, Texas campus to Anthropic, with the deal valued at approximately $9 billion. This marks one of the largest AI compute agreements involving a Bitcoin miner. This deal signifies a major convergence of AI infrastructure and cryptocurrency mining, as miners pivot to AI compute hosting to address the power crunch constraining AI data centers. It could accelerate the trend of Bitcoin miners transforming into power and compute providers for the AI industry. The reported agreement follows Anthropic's $19 billion, 20-year data center lease with Bitcoin miner TeraWulf on July 6. Riot's shares fell 5.4% on Monday but rose over 21% in overnight trading, and are up more than 53% year-to-date.

entry.title: Riot Platforms to Sell Bitcoin to Fund $9.1B AI Data Center Lease
entry.summary: Riot Platforms signed a 191 MW data center lease with an unnamed frontier AI lab, expecting $9.1 billion in gross contract revenue over a 20-year base term. The miner plans to continue selling Bitcoin from its treasury as a primary equity source, with construction costs estimated at $2.1-2.3 billion and rent not starting until December 2027 and June 2028. This marks another major Bitcoin miner pivoting toward AI infrastructure, accelerating the trend of mining companies diversifying away from pure Bitcoin production. It also introduces ongoing Bitcoin treasury sales as a financing mechanism, which could affect market supply dynamics and influence how other miners manage their holdings. Riot projects $2.1-$2.3 billion in capital spending, with 80-90% expected from long-term project debt that is not yet closed, leaving $210-$460 million in equity funding. A $573 million Morgan Stanley interim facility at SOFR plus 2.75% matures October 15, 2026, and an investment-grade backstop is still being finalized without disclosed terms.

entry.title: Ravencoin may roll back four days of transactions after critical flaw exploit
entry.summary: Ravencoin is attempting a chain rollback of roughly four days of transactions after attackers exploited a critical software flaw that allowed invalid blocks, with the first bad block appearing at height 4,487,776 on Aug. 7. Two mining pools, 2Miners and RavenMiner, are rebuilding the chain from block 4,487,775, while exchanges like Bitvavo and Upbit have halted RVN deposits and withdrawals. This is a significant proof-of-work governance and security incident: because a small number of pools dominate Ravencoin's hashpower, they can decide which version of history survives, potentially erasing payments users believed were final. It highlights how low-hashrate Bitcoin-derived networks are vulnerable to rollback-style attacks and how exchanges must react to protect against losses. The proposed rollback would reverse all transactions from block 4,487,776 onward, including payments and mining rewards from that window. Ravencoin released a fix but patching cannot undo already-written blocks; RavenMiner says it is running an emergency fix and will cover any payout shortfall itself, while it paused payouts until the chain settles.

entry.title: Nvidia's $500B AI infrastructure push widens gap with crypto compute
entry.summary: Nvidia has signed memorandums of understanding with Apollo Global Management, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to create financing platforms that could channel more than $500 billion into AI compute infrastructure. The company aims to establish AI compute as a bankable, long-lived infrastructure asset rather than a short-term technology expense. This move could dramatically expand centralized AI compute capacity, leaving decentralized crypto compute networks further behind in scale and competitiveness. It also signals a structural shift in how AI infrastructure is financed, with potential knock-on effects for blockchain-based compute marketplaces and AI-related crypto assets. The six Wall Street firms involved are Apollo Global Management, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield Asset Management, Goldman Sachs and KKR. NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang described the initiative as the first time technology chips have become an investable asset class, emphasizing that AI factories are revenue-generating, long-lived and fungible assets.

entry.title: Riot Platforms Surges 20% on $9.1B Anthropic AI Deal
entry.summary: Riot Platforms announced a $9.1 billion, 20-year agreement with AI lab Anthropic to repurpose its bitcoin mining infrastructure for AI computing, sending its stock up 20% in pre-market trading on August 11, 2026. The deal marks a landmark shift in the bitcoin mining industry, validating the repurposing of mining infrastructure for AI workloads. It could accelerate similar pivots by other miners and deepen the convergence between the crypto and AI sectors. The 20-year agreement is valued at $9.1 billion and involves converting Riot's mining racks for AI calculations. Riot's stock jumped about 20% in pre-market trading following the announcement.

entry.title: Riot Platforms Jumps 25% on Reported $9.1B AI Deal with Anthropic
entry.summary: Riot Platforms' stock surged 25% in after-hours trading on reports of a $9.1 billion AI deal with Anthropic. The contract includes two five-year extension options that could raise its potential value to $16.1 billion. The deal marks a major strategic crossover between Bitcoin mining and AI, potentially transforming how miners monetize their energy infrastructure. It highlights the growing demand for power and data-center capacity from AI firms and could influence how the broader crypto mining industry positions itself. The reported $9.1 billion base contract can be expanded to $16.1 billion through two five-year extension options. The deal has reportedly not been officially confirmed, and Riot Platforms is a vertically integrated U.S. Bitcoin miner with direct exposure to bitcoin prices.

entry.title: BTCPay Server Offers Bitcoin Bounty After Lightning Wallet Exploit
entry.summary: BTCPay Server announced a 10% bounty (capped at 3 BTC) for recovery of Bitcoin stolen in an exploit that abused LND admin macaroons, and is urging all users to update to version 2.4.2 immediately. The incident exposes real security risks in self-hosted Lightning Network infrastructure and directly affects operators who run vulnerable BTCPay/LND servers. It also underscores how open-source payment processors must prioritize rapid patching and rewarded vulnerability research to protect user funds. Attackers obtained LND admin macaroons, credentials that grant broad control over a Lightning node, and used them to access connected wallets. BTCPay has not disclosed how much Bitcoin was stolen or how many users were affected, and the bounty will be split among verified tips; the BTCPay Server Foundation is also donating 0.21 BTC each to researcher Craig Raw and the Bitcoin Red Team.

entry.title: Nasdaq to Acquire LeveL Markets in Push Toward Always-On Markets
entry.summary: Nasdaq has signed a definitive agreement to acquire LeveL Markets, the third-largest alternative trading system (ATS) in the US, and launched a new Digital Liquidity Networks (DLN) unit led by Roland Chai. The deal, announced on August 11, 2026, is subject to regulatory approval and financial terms were not disclosed. This acquisition marks a major institutional push into tokenized securities and 24/7 trading, directly bridging traditional market infrastructure with blockchain-based digital assets. It signals a growing convergence between conventional exchanges and crypto markets, potentially accelerating the adoption of tokenized assets among institutional investors. LeveL Markets processes hundreds of millions of shares daily, serves over 2,500 buy- and sell-side clients, and executes trades across more than 7,000 symbols, with average daily trading volume up 56% in 2025. Following the acquisition, LeveL will remain a FINRA-regulated ATS with its own management team, operating under Nasdaq's Digital Liquidity Networks. Nasdaq's earlier SEC filing proposed that tokenized stocks and ETFs trade alongside traditional shares via Depository Trust Company and blockchain settlement in a three-year pilot.

entry.title: BitMart founder denies exit scam as withdrawal freeze persists
entry.summary: BitMart founder Sheldon Xia publicly denied exit-scam rumors, saying the exchange 'has not disappeared, nor will we,' but offered no figures, timeline, or proof of reserves. Users report withdrawal requests stuck for weeks since the July 26 'orderly wind-down,' including a $10.1 million request. Weeks-long withdrawal failures at a major exchange raise serious solvency and fraud concerns, directly threatening user access to funds. This adds to broader distrust of centralized exchanges and could intensify scrutiny of counterparty risk across the crypto industry. On-chain data from Arkham Intelligence shows BitMart's tracked holdings fell from about $102 million on July 6 to $59.3 million, with the largest positions held in obscure tokens such as Ten Best Coins and WeFi rather than BTC, ETH, or stablecoins. The exchange's token BMX crashed 81% in a week, and the founder's statement provided no proof of reserves.

entry.title: BTCPay Server Supporters Offer Up to 3 BTC Bounty After Critical Exploit
entry.summary: BTCPay Server acknowledged a critical exploit that may have been AI-assisted, and credited Craig Raw and the Bitcoin Red Team fund for reporting the issue. Supporters have pledged up to 3 BTC as a recovery bounty. BTCPay Server is a widely used self-hosted Bitcoin payment processor, so a critical exploit could affect merchants and users who rely on it to accept Bitcoin directly. This incident also highlights the growing role of AI both in attacking and in defending open-source cryptocurrency infrastructure. Supporters have pledged up to 3 BTC as a recovery bounty, while BTCPay Server said the exploit may have been AI-assisted. The project credited Craig Raw and the Bitcoin Red Team fund for reporting the vulnerability.

entry.title: Ethereum's latest roadmap prioritizes privacy and quantum resistance, says Buterin
entry.summary: Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin published an updated roadmap called the "Strawmap" on Monday, elevating privacy, quantum resistance, and AI-assisted formal verification to top priorities. These new focus areas—including post-quantum scaling and native rollups—were not present in his 2023 roadmap. This signals a major strategic shift for Ethereum as it prepares for "Q-Day" and the potential threat of quantum computers, and it could reshape how the network handles privacy and scaling. Because Buterin is a core figure, this roadmap helps align the ecosystem's long-term research and development priorities, potentially affecting developers, validators, and users. The "Strawmap" deprioritizes VDFs and most EVM improvement work, and drops Verkle trees and state expiry in favor of new constructions. Buterin noted that Ethereum is increasingly relying on STARKs and AI-assisted formal verification to ensure protocol correctness, and he reiterated his "Lean Ethereum" vision of a quantum-safe, privacy-first, censorship-resistant, and performant protocol.

entry.title: Coldcard Seed-Phrase Hack Proves More Damaging Than Typical Crypto Breach
entry.summary: On July 30, 2026, a firmware vulnerability in Coldcard hardware wallets allowed attackers to drain roughly 1,082.65 BTC (about $70 million, with later estimates rising to $89 million) from over 1,000 addresses in a 41-minute sweep. Unlike typical hacks, this incident compromised seed phrases directly, making it far more damaging to users' ability to protect their funds. Hardware wallets are widely considered the most secure way to self-custody bitcoin, so a seed-phrase leak undermines the core promise of cold storage and threatens trust in the entire hardware-wallet ecosystem. Affected users must move funds to a newly generated seed phrase, and the industry may need to rethink supply-chain and firmware assurance. According to Bitcoin Magazine, the flaw also affects ephemeral keys, session keys in Clone Coldcard or Key Teleport features, and BIP 85 seeds derived from a compromised seed. Galaxy Research traced the July 30 sweep of 1,196 Bitcoin addresses and tied it to the firmware flaw; Bitcoin Magazine reports that roughly 1,000 BTC connected to the vulnerability has moved on-chain, and attacks are still ongoing.

entry.title: Mastercard closes $1.8B acquisition of stablecoin infra firm BVNK
entry.summary: Mastercard has closed its $1.8 billion acquisition of BVNK, a stablecoin infrastructure firm, after a competitive process that also involved Coinbase and Visa. BVNK reportedly chose Mastercard over a higher Coinbase offer of up to $2.5 billion because of cultural fit and strategic alignment. The deal shows major payments networks treating stablecoin infrastructure as strategically essential, not just a niche crypto service. It intensifies the race among Mastercard, Visa, Stripe, and Coinbase to control the rails of the roughly $300 billion stablecoin market. Early investor Concentric backed BVNK in 2019 at a $4 million valuation, making this a roughly 450x return on paper. The deal follows Stripe's $1.1 billion purchase of Bridge in late 2024, which pushed Mastercard and Visa to pursue stablecoin infrastructure deals.

entry.title: SharpLink posts $1B loss; $1.7B staked ETH treasury faces 90-day cash conversion
entry.summary: SharpLink reported a $1.08 billion net loss for the six months ending June 30, driven mostly by unrealized ETH price declines and impairments on LsETH and weETH. Its roughly $1.7 billion Ethereum treasury, largely staked, may take up to 90 days to fully convert to cash. This highlights the liquidity risk of staked Ethereum treasuries: even large ETH holders cannot instantly access funds when markets turn. It matters for sentiment around ETH and for public companies using staking to generate yield on crypto reserves. The loss included $827.7 million from unrealized ETH declines and $267.8 million from impairments of liquid staking and restaking tokens LsETH and weETH. As of Aug. 3, SharpLink held 888,938 unencumbered ETH-equivalent units, with ETH trading around $1,916.57 on Aug. 10, giving an illustrative gross value of roughly $1.7 billion.

entry.title: Crypto.com cancels CRO treasury deal, cuts rewards as CRO slides
entry.summary: Crypto.com terminated its proposed multi-billion dollar digital asset treasury (DAT) business combination with DJT/MCGA (Yorkville America) over the weekend and simultaneously cut cardholder cashback and staking rewards. CRO fell below $0.05, its lowest since October 2023, and a related ETF servicing deal with Yorkville was also scrapped. The termination and reward cuts signal operational and strategic stress at one of the largest crypto exchanges, directly affecting CRO token holders and card customers. The fraying relationship with a Trump-branded entity adds reputational and sentiment risks for Crypto.com and its ecosystem. Starting October 1, Ruby tier cashback drops from 2% to 1.5% and the monthly spending cap falls from $1,250 to $750, while Icy White loses unlimited 4% cashback for a 3.5% rate capped at $3,000. Staking rewards for Pro and Private lock-ups drop from 4% to 3% and 9% to 6% respectively on September 10, even though users' CRO remains locked.

entry.title: Coinsbuy Covers $7.9M Breach Loss, Offers $100K Reward
entry.summary: Crypto payments platform Coinsbuy suffered a security breach on Aug. 9 that drained more than $7.9 million across Ethereum and TRON. The company covered all affected client funds from its own reserves and is offering a $100,000 reward for information leading to the attacker. The incident underscores ongoing security risks for crypto payment platforms and custodial services. Coinsbuy's decision to reimburse users mitigated direct losses, but the attack highlights how stolen funds are laundered through privacy coins like Monero, complicating recovery and investigation. Blockchain investigators linked the attack to three addresses: two on Ethereum and one on TRON. BlockWatchdog reported about $6.34 million of the stolen funds flowed through FixedFloat exchange, while ChangeNOW helped freeze a six-figure portion; Coinsbuy replenished affected wallets with roughly $3.93 million shortly after the incident.

entry.title: Crypto lost $110M to hacks in July, Immunefi data shows
entry.summary: According to Immunefi, the crypto ecosystem lost roughly $110 million to hacks in July, while its audit competitions reportedly outperformed traditional tier-1 audits in finding vulnerabilities. The aggregate loss highlights persistent security risks in DeFi and the broader crypto market. It also suggests that competitive auditing models such as audit competitions may be becoming more effective at identifying vulnerabilities than conventional top-tier audits. Immunefi is a leading Web3 bug bounty platform, and its audit competitions are time-bound code reviews conducted by security researchers. The report compares these competitions with tier-1 audits, which are typically conducted by well-known firms.

entry.title: Hyperliquid RWA perps boom erodes revenue backing HYPE
entry.summary: Hyperliquid's open interest hit a record above $11 billion and 30-day volume reached nearly $178 billion, yet gross protocol revenue fell for a fourth straight quarter to about $202 million in Q2 2026. The gap stems from HIP-3 fee sharing, which now routes roughly half of perp volume through builder-deployed markets that keep up to half the trading fees. This reveals a structural shift in Hyperliquid's economics: record usage is increasingly unprofitable for the protocol because fee-sharing funnels revenue to external builders. Since the Assistance Fund's HYPE buyback is a fixed share of earnings, shrinking revenue means less HYPE is retired, directly weakening the earnings story that underpins token valuation. RWA perps on assets like gold, crude oil, Nvidia, Tesla, the Nasdaq-100 and pre-IPO SpaceX reached a record $3.6 billion in open interest and overtook bitcoin as Hyperliquid's largest perp market. However, Trade.xyz accounts for over 90% of HIP-3 open interest, and a single trade on a thin Korean pre-market venue dropped its SK Hynix contract 19% on Monday, triggering reimbursements.

entry.title: Crypto Dot-Com Shakeout: Over 100 Projects Fold in 2026
entry.summary: Over 100 crypto projects have shut down, filed for bankruptcy, or gone permanently dark in 2026, with four major firms opening closures within a single week in late July, including BitMEX, BitMart, Movement Labs, and Storj Labs. The shakeout is hitting crowded sectors like layer-2 networks and protocol tooling as altcoin prices drop 70% to 90% and token treasuries drain. This marks a maturity shift in crypto, from speculative token distribution to sustainable, cash-flow-positive business models. Projects that charge real fees in stablecoins or cash, like Aave, Hyperliquid, and Ether.fi, are surviving, which signals broader consolidation across DeFi, exchanges, and infrastructure. According to RootData, the pace of shutdowns is accelerating; the exits span exchanges, wallets, DeFi lending protocols, NFT marketplaces, and layer-1 blockchains, including Moonbeam, a Polkadot parachain that shut down on July 31. Over $1.1 billion was lost to exploits in the first half of 2026, and with venture rescue capital drying up, single hacks can force immediate bankruptcies while unmaintained 'zombie contracts' remain on-chain.

entry.title: Audited badges misleading crypto investors, Bybit hack shows
entry.summary: A new analysis argues that crypto 'audited' badges give investors a false sense of security, using Bybit's $1.46 billion exploit to show that audit findings miss non-code attack vectors. It cites research indicating that only a fraction of exploit losses originate in the code that conventional audits inspect. Because blockchain projects use audit badges as marketing signals, investors often equate 'audited' with 'safe,' which can distort risk perception and capital allocation across DeFi. The analysis may accelerate industry pressure for clearer audit scope labeling and stronger operational security practices. The article details that Bybit's Feb. 21, 2025 exploit involved a manipulated signing interface during a routine ETH transfer, after Safe revealed a compromised developer machine; external researchers found no vulnerability in Safe's contracts or front-end source. It also cites an Oak Security preprint that compared 23,818 audit findings with 218 rekt.news incidents representing $7.764 billion in losses, showing many incidents fall outside audited code.

entry.title: Circle Renews Coinbase USDC Deal as It Bets Big on Stablecoin Growth
entry.summary: Circle has renewed its USDC partnership with Coinbase, extending a key distribution arrangement for the second-largest stablecoin. The renewal comes as Circle intensifies its focus on stablecoin adoption and growth. The renewal secures a critical distribution channel for USDC, which underpins trading and payments across the crypto ecosystem. It also signals continued institutional commitment to stablecoins at a time when regulatory attention on the sector is increasing. USDC is a fully reserved stablecoin pegged to the U.S. dollar and issued by Circle, available on networks such as Ethereum, Base, and Polygon. The financial terms of the renewed deal were not disclosed, but the extended arrangement continues a partnership that has existed for several years.

entry.title: Kraken Nears Delisting Deadline for 21 Tokens, Holders Face Near-Zero Payouts
entry.summary: Kraken is approaching its deadline to delist 21 tokens, and holders who fail to act before the cutoff risk receiving payouts worth near zero. The exchange is removing all trading pairs for the affected assets. Delistings on major exchanges like Kraken often trigger sharp price drops because the token loses its primary liquidity venue. This event highlights the risk of holding low-liquidity or non-compliant assets that exchanges may periodically remove. When a token is delisted, all trading pairs are removed, and exchanges typically set a final date after which balances may be converted or liquidated. Affected holders should withdraw tokens to an external wallet before the deadline, as post-deadline payouts can be minimal.

entry.title: Bybit Expands Platform to Offer Stocks, ETFs, and Other Assets
entry.summary: Bybit has announced an expansion of its trading platform to include stocks, ETFs, and other assets beyond cryptocurrencies. The news was reported by Coinfomania, but specific details on the available instruments or launch timeline have not been disclosed. This move reflects the growing trend of crypto exchanges expanding into traditional financial assets, potentially broadening their user base and increasing trading volumes. It also positions Bybit to compete more directly with multi-asset platforms like Robinhood and eToro. The original article does not specify which stocks, ETFs, or other assets will be offered, nor does it provide a timeline or list of supported jurisdictions. Regulatory scrutiny may become a challenge, given that Bybit has faced warnings from financial regulators in multiple jurisdictions.
